checkpoint-sync download::beacon-node-ho.explain: Beacon node REST API to download the finalized state and block from, as a URL or `host:port` (then `http://` is assumed). Use a node you trust: the files become the starting point of your own node.

checkpoint-sync download::http-timeout.explain: Timeout for each HTTP request, as a Go duration. Mainnet states are several hundred megabytes, so raise it on slow links.

db query::bucket.explain: Name of the BoltDB bucket to scan, for example `blocks` or `state`. List the names with `prysmctl db buckets`.

db query::path.explain: Path to the BoltDB file itself, typically `<datadir>/beaconchaindata/beaconchain.db`, despite the flag description mentioning a directory. Stop the beacon node first: the command gives up after one second if the database is locked.
db query::path.caution: The file is opened read-write, and a missing file is created empty. Work on a copy if you are unsure.

db query::prefix.explain: Hex key prefix (with `0x`) to match in the bucket. Without it the command does nothing.

db query::print-keys.explain: Prints the matching keys. Printing values is not implemented, so a prefix scan fails unless this flag is set.

db buckets::path.explain: Accepted but not read: the command prints the bucket names compiled into this `prysmctl` version without opening any database.

db slasher-span-display::db-path-directo.explain: Directory that contains `slasher.db` (the slasher database of a beacon node running with `--slasher`). Required. Stop the beacon node first.

db slasher-span-display::validator-index.explain: Validator whose min or max spans are shown. Required.

db slasher-span-display::epoch.explain: Source epoch to show. The command displays the chunk containing this epoch. Required.

db slasher-span-display::chunk-kind.explain: `minspan` or `maxspan`: which of the two surround-vote span arrays to read.

db slasher-span-display::chunk-size.explain: Epochs per chunk. Must match the slasher parameters the database was written with; leave it unset to use the defaults.

db slasher-span-display::validator-chunk.explain: Validators per chunk. Must match the slasher parameters the database was written with; leave it unset to use the defaults.

db slasher-span-display::history-length.explain: Epochs of history the slasher keeps. Must match the slasher parameters the database was written with; leave it unset to use the defaults.

db slasher-span-display::display-all-val.explain: Shows a row for every validator stored in the same chunk, not only `--validator-index`.

db slasher-span-display::display-all-epo.explain: Shows every epoch of the chunk as columns, not only `--epoch`.

p2p send beacon-blocks-by-range::chain-c.explain: Chain config YAML for a custom network. Loaded after the network selection, so it overrides it.

p2p send beacon-blocks-by-range::peer-mu.explain: Peers to send the blocks-by-range request to, as comma-separated libp2p multiaddrs including the peer ID. Without it, the peers are read from the Prysm beacon node at `--prysm-api-endpoints`.

p2p send beacon-blocks-by-range::client-.explain: Local TCP port of the temporary libp2p host. Change it if 13001 is in use.
Local QUIC (UDP) port of the temporary libp2p host.

p2p send beacon-blocks-by-range::prysm-a.explain: gRPC endpoint(s) of Prysm beacon nodes. Always needed: the first one provides genesis and head information for the status handshake, and they supply peers when `--peer-multiaddrs` is not set.

p2p send beacon-blocks-by-range::start-s.explain: First slot requested. `0` means the first slot of the previous epoch, taken from the beacon node head.

p2p send beacon-blocks-by-range::network.explain: `mainnet`, `sepolia`, `holesky` or `hoodi`: sets fork digests and parameters so the handshake with the peer succeeds.

p2p send beacon-blocks-by-range::count.explain: Number of slots to request, starting at `--start-slot`.

p2p send beacon-blocks-by-range::step.explain: Slot step of the request. Recent specs deprecate `step` and expect `1`; other values are only useful for testing how peers respond.

p2p send blobs-by-range::chain-config-fi.explain: Chain config YAML for a custom network. Loaded after the network selection, so it overrides it.

p2p send blobs-by-range::peer-multiaddrs.explain: Peers to send the blob-sidecars-by-range request to, as comma-separated libp2p multiaddrs including the peer ID. Without it, the peers are read from the Prysm beacon node at `--prysm-api-endpoints`.

p2p send blobs-by-range::client-port-tcp.explain: Local TCP port of the temporary libp2p host. Change it if 13001 is in use.

p2p send blobs-by-range::client-port-qui.explain: Local QUIC (UDP) port of the temporary libp2p host.

p2p send blobs-by-range::prysm-api-endpo.explain: gRPC endpoint(s) of Prysm beacon nodes. Always needed: the first one provides genesis and head information for the status handshake, and they supply peers when `--peer-multiaddrs` is not set.

p2p send blobs-by-range::start-slot.explain: First slot requested. `0` means the first slot of the previous epoch, taken from the beacon node head.

p2p send blobs-by-range::count.explain: Number of slots whose blob sidecars are requested.
p2p send blobs-by-range::count.caution: This command has no `--network` flag and assumes mainnet unless you pass `--chain-config-file`. Since Fulu (PeerDAS), peers serve data columns instead of blob sidecars for new slots.

testnet generate-genesis::chain-config-f.explain: Chain config YAML (consensus-specs `config.yaml` format) of the new network. Required in practice: the command stops with `No chain config file was provided` without it.

testnet generate-genesis::deposit-json-f.explain: `deposit_data-*.json` from the deposit CLI. Its validators are placed in the genesis state instead of deterministically generated ones.

testnet generate-genesis::num-validators.explain: Number of validators generated from the well-known interop keys (insecure, test only). The flag is required even with `--deposit-json-file`.

testnet generate-genesis::genesis-time.explain: Genesis Unix timestamp in seconds. If unset, the timestamp of `--geth-genesis-json-in` is used, and failing that the current time.

testnet generate-genesis::genesis-time-d.explain: Seconds added to the genesis time, which gives you time to start the nodes before the chain begins.

testnet generate-genesis::override-eth1d.explain: Sets the state's `eth1_data` from block 0 of the execution client at `--execution-endpoint` (with an empty deposit tree).

testnet generate-genesis::geth-genesis-j.explain: Execution genesis (`genesis.json`) to base the network on. Its fork times (Shanghai, Cancun, Prague, Osaka) are rewritten to match the chain config and genesis time. Post-merge forks require `baseFeePerGas` in the file.
Where to write the resulting execution `genesis.json`. Initialize your execution client with this file so both layers agree on genesis.

testnet generate-genesis::execution-endp.explain: Execution client JSON-RPC URL, used only with `--override-eth1data`.

testnet generate-genesis::fork.explain: Fork whose `BeaconState` layout the genesis uses, for example `electra` or `fulu`. It should match the fork active at epoch 0 in your chain config.

testnet generate-genesis::output-ssz.explain: Output path for the SSZ-encoded state, the format beacon nodes load with `--genesis-state`. At least one output flag is required.

testnet generate-genesis::output-yaml.explain: Output path for a YAML dump of the state, for inspection.

testnet generate-genesis::output-json.explain: Output path for a JSON dump of the state, for inspection.

weak-subjectivity checkpoint::beacon-nod.explain: Trusted beacon node REST API. Prysm nodes answer from their weak subjectivity endpoint; for other clients the checkpoint is computed from the head state. Prints a `--weak-subjectivity-checkpoint=<root>:<epoch>` value for the beacon node.

weak-subjectivity checkpoint::http-timeo.explain: Timeout for each HTTP request. Raise it if the fallback path has to download a full state from a slow node.

validator withdraw::beacon-node-host.explain: REST API of a synced beacon node that receives the signed messages, as `host:port` or a URL.

validator withdraw::path.explain: A JSON file, or a directory searched for `.json` files, containing signed BLS-to-execution changes (the `bls_to_execution_change-*.json` output of the deposit CLI). Files that are not such lists are skipped with a warning.

validator withdraw::confirm.explain: Confirms that you checked the withdrawal addresses. Required together with `--accept-terms-of-use`; without both, the command prints a warning and stops.
validator withdraw::confirm.caution: Once included on chain, the withdrawal address cannot be changed. Check every address before you run this.

validator withdraw::verify-only.explain: Does not submit anything: only checks whether the messages in `--path` are in the beacon node's operation pool. Messages already included in a block are no longer in the pool, so check a block explorer too.

validator withdraw::config-file.explain: YAML file with values for this command's flags (keys are flag names). Flags on the command line win.

validator withdraw::accept-terms-of-use.explain: Accepts the Prysm terms of use. This command requires it on every run, together with `--confirm`.

validator proposer-settings::config-file.explain: YAML file with values for this command's flags. Flags on the command line win.

validator proposer-settings::default-fee.explain: Fee recipient written to `default_config` of the generated file. Only used with `--output-proposer-settings-path`; if omitted there, you are prompted for it.

validator proposer-settings::token.explain: The validator's Keymanager API token (contents of its `--keymanager-token-file`). Required.

validator proposer-settings::validator-h.explain: URL of the running validator's HTTP API (started with `--rpc`). Required: you must pass it even for the default `http://127.0.0.1:7500`.

validator proposer-settings::output-prop.explain: Writes the validator's current fee recipients as a proposer settings JSON file you can pass to `--proposer-settings-file`. Without it, the command only prints them. Gas limits and builder options are not exported.

validator exit::wallet-dir.explain: Prysm wallet holding the keys to exit. You must pass it explicitly (or use the Web3Signer flags); the default location is not assumed.

validator exit::wallet-password-file.explain: File with the wallet password, to skip the prompt. A trailing newline is ignored.

validator exit::account-password-file.explain: Accepted for compatibility; exits are signed with keys from the unlocked wallet, so only the wallet password is needed.

validator exit::public-keys.explain: Validators to exit, as comma-separated hex public keys. Without it (and without `--exit-all`) you pick them interactively.

validator exit::beacon-rpc-provider.explain: gRPC `host:port` of a synced beacon node (its `--rpc-port`, default 4000). The command refuses to run while that node is syncing.

validator exit::validators-external-sign.explain: Signs the exits with Web3Signer instead of a local wallet. Pass it with `--validators-external-signer-public-keys`.
Web3Signer keys available for the exit: a comma-separated list or a public keys URL.

validator exit::grpc-max-msg-size.explain: Maximum gRPC response size in bytes. The default is effectively unlimited.

validator exit::tls-cert.explain: Certificate to verify the beacon node's gRPC TLS certificate, if it serves TLS.

validator exit::grpc-headers.explain: Extra `key=value` gRPC metadata, comma-separated, for example an auth header for a proxy.

validator exit::grpc-retries.explain: Retries for a failed gRPC call before giving up.

validator exit::grpc-retry-delay.explain: Base delay between gRPC retries (linear backoff).

validator exit::exit-all.explain: Selects every key in the wallet or remote signer. You still have to confirm unless `--force-exit` is set.
validator exit::exit-all.caution: Exits are irreversible. Check the printed key list before confirming.

validator exit::force-exit.explain: Skips the final `continue with the voluntary exit? (y/n)` confirmation, for scripts.
validator exit::force-exit.caution: Combined with `--exit-all`, this exits every key without any prompt.

validator exit::exit-json-output-dir.explain: Writes each signed exit to a JSON file in this directory instead of broadcasting it. Still needs a synced beacon node to sign.
validator exit::exit-json-output-dir.caution: A signed exit stays valid. Anyone who gets the file can broadcast it.

validator exit::mainnet.explain: Signs the exit for mainnet (the default). Use the network your validators run on; only one network flag can be set.

validator exit::sepolia.explain: Signs the exit for Sepolia. Use the network your validators run on; only one network flag can be set.

validator exit::holesky.explain: Signs the exit for Holesky (being retired). Use the network your validators run on; only one network flag can be set.

validator exit::hoodi.explain: Signs the exit for Hoodi. Use the network your validators run on; only one network flag can be set.

validator exit::accept-terms-of-use.explain: Accepts the terms of use without the interactive prompt. Pass it in scripts and other non-interactive runs.
